title: Kernel auto-selection v2 (Runtime 1.21) — Rollout checklist (Staging → Canary → GA)
text:
Kernel auto-selection v2 (Runtime 1.21) — Rollout checklist (Staging → Canary → GA)

Purpose
- This checklist is the execution guardrail for rolling out Kernel auto-selection v2 (selector v2) in Runtime 1.21 across Hosted, then Dedicated, and finally Private.
- Primary goals: (1) reduce p95/p99 latency + improve throughput stability on heterogeneous fleets (A100/H100/L40S), (2) preserve correctness + determinism guarantees, (3) ensure rapid rollback and safe overrides for customer escalations.

Definitions / quick references
- “v2” = kernel auto-selection v2 decision logic + GPU SKU aware registry + feature extraction (model family + seq-length regime) + allow/deny rules + telemetry.
- “v1” = existing selector behavior (baseline).
- “Gate” = control-plane controlled feature flag + runtime config plumbing.
- “Allowlist/Denylist” = per-model and per-(model, GPU SKU, driver/CUDA) rules for enabling/disabling v2 or specific kernels.
- Rollback runbook: Confluence: eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/kernel-selection-v2-override-and-rollback-runbook

Owners (for rollout execution)
- Program / comms: Talia Benson
- Release train: Connor O’Brien
- CI/perf validation: Sahana Iyer, Marcus Reed
- SLO + rollback triggers: Aisha Bello, Allison Grant
- Tail latency + telemetry: Omar El‑Sayed
- Selector logic: Yuki Sato
- Control plane gates + policy engine: Ethan Park, Benji Okafor, Jordan Lee

0) Pre-flight (must be complete before ANY environment enablement)
[ ] Code landed behind gate (no default-on behavior)
    - Confirm Runtime 1.21 build contains: feature gate plumbing, allow/deny rules hot reload, telemetry + sampling controls, determinism tests.
    - Required PRs merged: pr-28460, pr-28466, pr-28473, pr-28510 (and pr-28522 if long-context guardrail required for this train).
    - Owner: Connor / Yuki

[ ] Determinism & replayability checks green
    - CI job for deterministic replay passes on at least 2 SKUs (A100, H100) and one “other” (L40S) if available.
    - Selection decision invariant: identical inputs → identical chosen kernel, candidates ordering stable, feature extraction stable.
    - Owner: Noah Patel / Jordan Lee

[ ] Telemetry schema + cardinality review completed
    - Fields present (minimum): selector_version, model_family, model_id (stable), model_revision, gpu_sku_normalized, cuda_version, driver_version, seq_bucket, prefill_tokens, decode_tokens, chosen_kernel, fallback_reason (if any), candidates_count, decision_latency_us, selection_cache_hit (if applicable).
    - Sampling policy configured (default: low sampling on full candidate lists; always-on counters for chosen kernel distribution).
    - Confirm no PII in traces/logs.
    - Owner: Omar / Logan Wright / Caleb Johnson

[ ] Dashboards live + queries verified
    - Dashboard panels:
      - selection distribution over time by model family + GPU SKU + seq bucket
      - p50/p95/p99 latency deltas v2 vs v1 (split prefill/decode if available)
      - error rates (5xx, timeouts), OOMs, kernel launch failures
      - fallback rate + fallback reasons
      - decision overhead (selector eval time)
    - Validate against known issue INT-10411 (metric cardinality). Ensure queries use normalized labels.
    - Owner: Allison / Aisha

[ ] Denylist/guardrails reviewed (known-bad combos)
    - Explicit denies for:
      - unstable kernels on specific SKUs
      - known-bad driver/CUDA combos (if applicable; see pr-28495 guardrail)
      - long-context edge cases if not yet fixed (historical: long-context prefill mis-selection)
    - Confirm GPU SKU normalization mapping covers A100 variants, MIG naming, and cloud instance aliases.
    - Owner: Isabella Rossi / Benji

[ ] Benchmark coverage meets minimum bar
    - At least: Llama + Mistral + Qwen + Gemma families, short + medium + long context, mixed workloads.
    - Confirm perf suite + canary scenarios updated.
    - Owner: Marcus Reed / Claire Dubois / Rina Kobayashi

[ ] Rollback is proven (not just documented)
    - Dry run rollback in a non-prod environment: disable v2 by model in a single region, verify config propagates, selection reverts to v1, latency returns to baseline.
    - Validate “pin kernel” override works and can be removed cleanly.
    - Owner: SRE oncall delegate + Yuki + Ethan

[ ] Oncall brief delivered (30 min)
    - Walkthrough: what metrics matter, what “bad” looks like, how to disable quickly, who to page.
    - Provide a short cheat-sheet (copy/paste commands + config keys).
    - Owner: Talia / Omar / Aisha

1) Staging rollout (internal / pre-prod)
Goal: validate correctness + telemetry + config propagation without customer impact.

[ ] Enable v2 in staging for representative model set (min 4)
    - Include one long-context heavy model, one embeddings-like short prompt pattern if applicable, one chat default.
    - Owner: Ethan / Benji

[ ] Staging acceptance criteria (hold for 24h)
    - Correctness: no increase in request failures attributable to kernel selection; no kernel launch error spikes.
    - Perf: p99 not worse than v1 by >2% on long-context buckets; p95 not worse than v1 by >3% overall.
    - Fallbacks: fallback rate within expected band (target: <1% steady-state; investigate any >3%).
    - Telemetry: event volumes within budget; no ingestion/backpressure.
    - Owner: Omar / Marcus

[ ] Sign-off to proceed to Hosted canary
    - Runtime kernels: Hiro Tanaka (or delegate)
    - Runtime perf/correctness: Noah Patel
    - SRE: Aisha Bello
    - Release: Connor O’Brien

2) Hosted Canary rollout (production, limited scope)
Goal: measure real traffic behavior and tail latency effects; ensure fast rollback.

Setup
[ ] Canary window scheduled + staffed
    - Named “rollback authority” on calendar (single decision maker). Default: Aisha; backup: Connor.
    - Runtime engineer on point: Yuki; backup: Grace.
    - Owner: Talia

[ ] Canary cohort defined
    - Start with: 1 region, 1–5% traffic for allowlisted models.
    - Prefer models with stable traffic + clear SLO baselines.
    - Exclude any models currently under incident or unusual traffic.
    - Owner: Benji / Ethan

Enablement
[ ] Turn on v2 via gate for cohort
[ ] Confirm within 15 min: selection distribution matches expectation (no “all traffic to fallback”).
[ ] Confirm telemetry sampling is as configured (no unexpected cardinality).

Hosted Canary gates (must hold for 6–24h depending on traffic volume)
[ ] Error budget / reliability gates
    - 5xx rate: no regression >0.05pp vs baseline for cohort
    - timeout rate: no regression >0.02pp
    - OOM / kernel launch errors: no sustained increase

[ ] Performance gates
    - Overall p95 latency: improvement expected; no regression >2% allowed
    - Overall p99 latency: no regression >1% allowed (hard stop if >3% for 15 min)
    - Long-context bucket p99: no regression >2% allowed; rollback trigger if >5% for 10 min
    - Throughput stability: no increased variance vs baseline (use perf-canary derived metric if available)

[ ] Selector overhead gates
    - Decision latency overhead within budget (target: <50µs p95; investigate >150µs p95)
    - CPU overhead not materially increasing runtime CPU saturation.

Escalation / rollback triggers (Hosted)
- Immediate rollback if any of:
  - kernel launch failures spike and correlate with v2 enablement
  - p99 regression >5% for long-context buckets sustained 10 min
  - error rate regression breaches SLO gate
  - fallback storms (fallback_reason dominated by “missing kernel” or “unstable kernel”) implying mapping/config issue

[ ] Canary exit criteria met and recorded
    - Include snapshot links: dashboards, cohort definition, allow/deny rules used, final metrics summary.
    - Owner: Omar / Talia

3) Expansion (Hosted broad enablement)
[ ] Expand allowlist to additional models in same region (stepwise)
[ ] Expand to additional regions (one at a time)
[ ] Confirm denylist remains current (no new SKUs/drivers introduced without review)
[ ] Confirm support readiness: update internal troubleshooting macros + known issues doc

4) Dedicated rollout (reserved capacity pools)
Goal: avoid surprises on constrained GPU SKUs and customer-specific driver stacks.

Pre-requisites
[ ] Dedicated pool GPU inventory confirmed (SKUs, MIG usage, driver/CUDA)
[ ] Any pool with “non-standard” driver stack reviewed explicitly (default to v2 off if unknown)
[ ] Customer comms prepared for impacted customers (if any)

Dedicated rollout steps
[ ] Start with one internal dogfood dedicated pool
[ ] Then one low-risk external pool (w/ customer approval if required)
[ ] Enable per-model allowlist only; do NOT blanket-enable pool-wide on first pass

Dedicated acceptance criteria
[ ] No latency regressions on the customer’s key routes (use their workload profile if provided)
[ ] No increase in tail-latency variability during peak hours
[ ] Rollback validated in dedicated context (confirm config propagation path differs from Hosted)

5) Private readiness (VPC / on-prem)
Goal: ensure we can support constrained hardware + manual ops.

[ ] Docs ready
    - Override instructions (pin kernel / disable v2) in customer-facing format
    - Troubleshooting steps for SKU normalization mismatches
    - Known-issues list updated with mitigations

[ ] Support plan
    - Escalation channel defined (Runtime kernels + SRE)
    - SLA expectations aligned for “runtime upgrade + v2 enablement”

6) GA criteria (formal)
GA means: default-on for eligible cohorts OR widely enabled behind stable policy with minimal exceptions.

[ ] Reliability: 2 weeks with no v2-caused Sev-1/Sev-2 incidents
[ ] Performance: median improvements observed and documented; tail lat not worse in any major bucket
[ ] Denylist stable and reviewed weekly during rollout; process in place for emergency deny additions
[ ] Determinism: no open correctness/determinism bugs
[ ] Runbook validated (at least one real-world rollback or a successful drill)
[ ] Release notes ready + reviewed (runtime 1.21 entry includes how to disable/pin)

7) Final sign-offs
